title: Your Ability to Cope with Stress Changes with the Seasons and Your Own Biological Clocks - Nautilus
gist: A short piece argues stress resilience is a dynamic, seasonally fluctuating state rather than a fixed personal trait, citing winter energy/immune/social dips versus spring and summer highs.

insights.claim: Stress resilience should be understood as a dynamic balance that shifts across the year rather than a fixed personal trait.
insights.speaker: Masha Remskar
insights.so_what: Reframes stress/resilience research and wellness product design (apps, coaching) around seasonal cycles rather than static personality traits.
insights.quote: Stress resilience is a dynamic balance rather than a fixed trait

insights.claim: During winter, people's energy levels drop, immune function is impaired, social engagement declines, and adherence to exercise routines falls, according to cited research.
insights.speaker: Masha Remskar
insights.so_what: Consumer health and fitness engagement (gym attendance, wellness app usage) likely has a predictable seasonal trough in winter months.
insights.locator: During winter, your energy tends to dip

insights.claim: Spring's longer daylight hours are associated with a subjective sense of increased energy, while summer is reported as the most active and social season of the year.
insights.speaker: Masha Remskar
insights.so_what: Supports a seasonal demand curve for fitness, social, and travel-related consumer activity peaking in summer.
